newsitem.title: USA: Integrated Process sees FY97 revs off FY96.
newsitem.headline: Integrated Process sees FY97 revs off FY96.

text.p: Integrated Process Equipment Corp, a maker of semiconductor process equipment, said Thursday if the industry's current slowdown continues its fiscal 1997's sales may be below fiscal 1996's $184.5 million.

Earlier, Integrated Process reported a net loss of $0.23 per share on revenues of $32 million for fiscal 1997's first quarter ended September 30, versus a net profit of $0.20 a share on sales of $38 million one year ago.
"This decrease was primarily attributable to a shortfall in revenues from sulfuric acid reprocessors and plasma jet systems," the company said in a statement.

Integrated Process said it will cut staff, especially at units developing products that are exclusive of the company's chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) machines, which made up about 88 percent of sales in the first quarter.
First quarter results include an accrual for these reductions, which will be completed by the end of the Company's second fiscal quarter ending December 31, 1996.
Integrated Proces also has decided to focus near term process and applications engineering efforts on its advanced high-throughput CMP tool, the AvantGAARD 676.

To date, the 676 has been used solely for metal polishing, but the company recently has demonstrated the feasibility of polishing oxide layers with this tool, and the process is being qualified by several leading semiconductor makers.
"Integrated Process will have the ability to address the market's requirement for both oxide and metal CMP with one machine," Chief Executive Sanjeev Chitre said in a statement.
The company has over 40,676 of the AvantGAARD 676 machines installed and in production worldwide for metal planarization.
